svg.aria-label: How to write 酒: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 酒
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 酒 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 酒.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E9%85%92.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 酒, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece as 洗 opens: two dots, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–10 draw the right side as 西 is written, with one stroke more: a horizontal, the box's left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a left-falling stroke and a vertical that bends right without lifting, both from above the box, a short horizontal across the inside, then the horizontal that closes the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto runs the box's right side straight down past the bottom horizontal, where the source's turns in to the left at the foot.
